title: Omnidirectional pick-and-place robot
summary: A modular mecanum-wheel robot with four-link suspension and a guided scoop-and-lift mechanism.
description: A five-person MCTR 260 team designed a robot to collect and deliver balls and blocks in a simulated warehouse. Kalen led mechanical design; the team developed the control and perception systems.
objectives: Create a modular chassis with replaceable suspension and lifting modules.
Keep object handling predictable enough to support the team’s autonomous navigation.
contributions: Led mechanical design and developed the four-link suspension modules using adjustable RC coilovers.
Conceived the bevel-gear-driven lead screw and guided scoop, which stays level during lifting and tips at the top.
Guided teammates new to CAD through the design of the mechanism’s components.

process.title: Modularity as a starting point
process.body: Defined mounting interfaces let the chassis, suspension, and lifting subsystems evolve independently. Two mirrored suspension configurations serve all four wheel positions.

process.title: Tune contact, simplify manufacture
process.body: Adjustable RC coilovers replaced mismatched kit shocks. The report documents 15.28 mm of suspension travel and 45 × 45 mm M4 mounting patterns for the suspension.

process.title: Make unloading mechanical
process.body: A bevel gear pair turns the lead screw through 90°. Guide rails keep the scoop level through travel and passively tip it at the top, reducing control complexity.

results: Team placed first out of 20 teams and received the innovation award, according to Kalen’s project notes.
The final report describes autonomous collection of nearly every object, with manual intervention for the last object.
lessons: Simple mechanisms and early system testing improved reliability.
Modular interfaces made iteration and assembly more manageable.
